## Summary

Trim pass (#1176): measured where gate time goes, then cut what the measurement showed. Builds quality#acceptance-test-cpu-budget. quality#acceptance-gate-time-targets stays planned (director, option b: the full gate is not gated in this lane); the fast-tier quiet runs and the full gate before and after are below.

- #1177 measurement, no product file: table on #1176 (issuecomment-7032763700); internal-seam list on #1119.
- #1182 (#687) the per-test CPU budget fails the gate: a new or changed integration item over gate-budget.toml test_cpu_seconds is measured again once, alone, and fails the run only when over both times, naming the test, both CPU times and the budget; an e2e item is never held; unchanged items are reported only. Changed means differing from the merge base with the default branch (local refs, no network), plus test files that directly import a changed in-repo file. Shared prepared state is billed to its own line. Same rule in templates/python's conftest copy.
- #1181 (#692, cut to what was measured) one check-gate-free process answers both justfile backticks: about 0.04 to 0.06 s CPU less per nested `just` run, -2.3% CPU over the 29 kit tests that run just in a kit copy.
- #1180 test_seeded's set-up: nested gates without an xdist worker, the kit's node_modules copied into its kit copy, tool homes asked once: 10.0 s to 7.5 s CPU alone. The other five slow-from-set-up items were measured: sharing would save nothing; each remaining cost is named on #1180's report.
- #1178 reverted (director decision b): mapping sandboxed items needs coverage data out of the qc sandbox, which ADR 0022 forbids; what was tried and why each failed is on #1178. ADR 0022 unchanged.
- #1179 closed with no change: one qc sandbox start is 0.91 s CPU (not 1.5); cuts within policy and proof are at most 5% (profile on #1179).
- Pre-commit hook not built: moved from #1183 to standalone #1186, waiting on the owner's decision on the slot rule (below).

## Validation

- Quiet-box window (director held every other lane), head 19f970a6, map written by `just fast-map` at that head (628.8 s wall, 3,967 s CPU, load1 7.9 to 5.9; 43 sandboxed items fail under coverage, as on main):
  - one-script `just fast` (scripts/octo-feather-spec-status), 53 items, all green: 56.9 s wall / 162.6 s CPU, load1 5.87 to 3.88; 55.9 s / 163.5 s, load1 2.78 to 4.14; 54.7 s / 142.7 s, load1 2.96 to 3.01. All three under 90 s.
- Full gate, not gated here: before, median 474.4 s over 3 green runs on main trees (9077, 9094, 9968; load1 7 to 15), item CPU sum 2,193 s; after, 330.8 s at 19f970a6 (load1 4.0 to 9.3) and 316.8 s at 94953f6b (load1 8.8 to 10.5), item CPU sum 1,969 s (-10%). Load differed between the sets; CPU is the fairer comparison and still moves 15 to 50% run to run (#1182's measurement).
- Final head b35abd97: full gate 422 passed (343.5 s), recorded pass; `just qc` passed acceptance-test-cpu-budget (3/3 tagged cases).
- CI red on 94953f6b, now repaired: the cpu_budget.py test of ticket 1182 linked the kit's node_modules into its kit copy; under CI=true the nested gate's pnpm install reinstalled the kit's own through the link and concurrent sandbox items found srt missing (51 failures). Now a real copy; proved on a fresh clone with CI=true. Also fixed a pre-existing install-check quoting bug it surfaced (justfile:447, #689: NameError instead of the srt MISSING message).
- Owner decisions for the merge: the hook (#1186) vs the heavy slot (the template hook runs `just fast` on every commit; a one-script kit `just fast` selects ~53 items, over heavy_items 30, so inside an agent each commit would need the heavy slot): (a) hook as the template has it, slot rule unchanged; (b) the slot counts only test items, fast tier cut under 30 (not reachable for most scripts); (c) fast-tier runs exempt from the heavy slot (a spec call on the slot rule); (d) defer the hook to its own lane. Supervisor recommends (c), built in a follow-up lane after this merge. ADR 0022 exception (option a on #1178) is available if the owner wants sandboxed items mapped.
- Advisory model judgment on acceptance-test-cpu-budget (no gate reads it): does-not-show, confidence 1.000, uncalibrated; the evidence record holds the tagged cases' commands and pass, not their output text.
